<implementation-notes>
IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
Architecture: This is a pure infrastructure packaging feature — no application code changes. All files are declarative YAML/Dockerfile with no business logic.

Dockerfile Strategy: Multi-stage build with workspace root context. The Go workspace (go.work) with replace directives requires all modules (internal/common/, operators/keystone/, operators/c5c3/) to be available at build time. Build stage copies go.work, go.sum files first for layer caching, then copies source directories. Runtime stage is distroless/static:nonroot for minimal attack surface.

Helm Chart Design: Standard kubebuilder-style operator chart. values.yaml exposes operational knobs without exposing template complexity. _helpers.tpl follows Helm best practices with standard label/selector helpers. CRD is in crds/ directory (not templates/) so Helm installs it before templates, avoiding chicken-and-egg issues.

RBAC Derivation: ClusterRole rules are manually derived from kubebuilder RBAC markers in keystone_controller.go. This is a one-time manual step since we don't have make manifests generating the Helm chart. Future CI should validate RBAC rules match markers.

Webhook Configuration: Both MutatingWebhookConfiguration and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration reference the operator Service for webhook callbacks. cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from annotation enables automatic CA bundle injection from cert-manager Certificate resource. Webhook port is 9443 (container) mapped to 443 (Service).

FluxCD Integration: HelmRelease follows the established pattern (memcached-operator.yaml as reference). dependsOn ensures cert-manager (for TLS), mariadb-operator (for Database/User/Grant CRDs), and memcached-operator (for Memcached CRDs) are ready before keystone-operator starts.

Key Pitfalls:
1. Build context must be workspace root, not operators/keystone/ — the go.work replace directive breaks otherwise
2. RBAC rules must exactly match kubebuilder markers — events only gets create;patch, external-secrets resources don't get delete
3. Webhook service name in configurations must match the Service created by the chart
4. Health probe port 8081 is hardcoded in bootstrap.Run() defaults — not configurable via values
5. CRD copy must be exact — no manual modifications that would diverge from generated source

Data Flow:
```
FluxCD → reconciles HelmRelease → Helm installs CRDs (crds/) → Helm renders templates → K8s creates resources → cert-manager injects CA → operator starts → reconciles Keystone CRs
```

Component Relationships:
```
Dockerfile ──builds──> container image
                           │
values.yaml ──configures──> templates/ ──renders──> K8s resources
                           │
Chart.yaml ──metadata──> Helm chart
                           │
FluxCD HelmRelease ──deploys──> Helm chart ──into──> openstack namespace
```
</implementation-notes>

  <purpose>Condensed language-agnostic rules for production-quality code</purpose>

  <section name="error-handling">
    <rule id="ERR-1">NEVER return sentinel values (None, -1, empty string) to indicate errors — raise/return an error</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-2">Chain or wrap exceptions to preserve the original cause and stack trace</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-3">Catch the most specific exception type possible — never bare except/catch-all</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-4">Include context in error messages: what operation failed, with which inputs, and why</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-5">Never silently swallow exceptions — log + re-raise, or handle explicitly</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="architecture">
    <rule id="ARCH-1">Services orchestrate workflows — no business logic in controllers/handlers, no HTTP/CLI concerns in services</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-2">Repositories return domain objects, not ORM models or raw dicts</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-3">Domain layer has zero imports from infrastructure, API, or framework code</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-4">Use dependency injection — pass dependencies as constructor/function parameters, never import and instantiate inline</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-5">One function, one responsibility — if you describe a function with "and", split it</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="async-concurrency">
    <rule id="ASYNC-1">NEVER call blocking I/O (file reads, HTTP requests, sleep) inside async functions — use async equivalents or run in a thread pool</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-2">Use the language-appropriate wrapper for unavoidable blocking code in async contexts (run_in_executor, goroutines, worker threads)</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-3">Never fire-and-forget async tasks — always await, collect, or track them for error handling</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-4">Use async-safe primitives for shared state — async locks, channels, or atomic operations</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-5">Limit concurrency for external calls with semaphores or worker pools — unbounded parallelism causes resource exhaustion</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="data-modeling">
    <rule id="DATA-1">Use the simplest appropriate type — plain function before class, flat struct before nested hierarchy</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-2">Use immutable types for value objects — frozen dataclasses, readonly structs, Object.freeze</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-3">Validate at system boundaries (API input, config loading, file parsing) — trust internal data</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-4">Prefer enums over string constants for fixed sets of values — catches typos at compile/import time</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="resource-management">
    <rule id="RES-1">Use context managers, defer, try-finally, or using blocks for ALL resources (files, connections, locks, temp files)</rule>
    <rule id="RES-2">Clean up partial state on failure — delete created files, rollback transactions, release reservations</rule>
    <rule id="RES-3">Set explicit timeouts on ALL external calls (HTTP, database, queues) — no call should block indefinitely</rule>
  </section>

## Description

When comparing a caller-constructed Kubernetes resource spec against an API-server-stored spec, the desired spec must be deep-copied and normalized to fill in API-server defaults before the comparison. This prevents infinite update loops caused by zero-value fields in the caller's spec differing from defaulted fields in the stored spec. The comparison uses the normalized copy, but the update (if needed) writes the original spec to let the API server apply its own defaults. Both pod-level defaults (ServiceAccountName, DNSPolicy, SchedulerName, TerminationGracePeriodSeconds, EnableServiceLinks) and container-level defaults (ImagePullPolicy, TerminationMessagePath, TerminationMessagePolicy) must be normalized.

The normalization functions live in the shared `normalize` package (`internal/common/normalize/`) and are imported by both `deployment` and `job` packages. This avoids code duplication and ensures a single source of truth for the defaulting logic.


```go

normalize.PodSpecDefaults(&desiredSpec.Template.Spec)

if !apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(existing.Spec, *desiredSpec) {
```

Each install_* function follows a consistent pattern: (1) check if the tool is already installed at the correct version (skip if so), (2) download the binary to a temporary directory, (3) verify SHA256 checksum via a shared verify_sha256 helper, (4) install with 0755 permissions.     <name>Chainsaw E2E test suite structure with JMESPath condition assertions</name>
```
    <component>tests/e2e/*/</component>
    <category>testing</category>
    <applies-when>Adding a new Chainsaw E2E test suite for an operator or infrastructure component</applies-when>
    <content>
## Description

Each Chainsaw E2E test file follows a fixed structure: (1) SPDX Apache-2.0 header, (2) descriptive comment block listing what the test validates and referencing requirement IDs with feature ID (e.g., REQ-001, REQ-012 (CC-0016)), (3) apiVersion chainsaw.kyverno.io/v1alpha1 kind Test, (4) spec with namespace (for namespaced tests) and timeouts.assert: 5m (overriding the global 120s for full reconciliation cycles), (5) numbered steps with '# ── Step N: Description ──' comment headers, each containing a try block. Condition assertions use JMESPath filter syntax (conditions[?type == 'X']) with string status values ('True'/'False') and reason strings. Numeric comparisons use CEL backtick-quoted literals (e.g., (availableReplicas > `0`)). Error assertions verify resource non-existence via the error step. Script steps use 'set -euo pipefail' for multi-command scripts and include explicit timeout overrides for long-running operations.
```
